channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Valdemar nega ter cota de emendas, e diz só sugerir destino do dinheiro
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the Liberal Party, denied having a quota or authority over the allocation of parliamentary amendments, stating he only makes political suggestions after consultations with various societal actors. The statement was made in a submission to the Federal Supreme Court on Monday, July 20, 2026. The report will be updated with additional information.

item.title: Número de eleitores com menos de 18 anos cai 14,5% em 2026
item.description: The Brazilian electorate for the 2026 elections totals 158.7 million eligible voters, with a 13.9% increase in the 60+ age group (from 32.8 to 37.4 million) and a 14.5% decrease among those 18 or younger (from 4.1 to 3.5 million). Women make up 53% of the electorate, men 47%. Voting is optional for ages 16–18 and mandatory from 18 onward.

item.title: PSD oficializa candidatura de Eduardo Paes ao governo do Rio
item.description: The PSD officially nominated Eduardo Paes as its candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, with lawyer Jane Reis (MDB) as his running mate for vice-governor. Paes, a four-time mayor of Rio and current poll leader, has the support of President Lula and is making his third bid for state office. The ticket also includes federal deputies Pedro Paulo (PSD) and Benedita da Silva (PT) as Senate candidates.

item.title: O que provocou a mudança de estratégia na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) campaign is shifting strategy amid multiple crises, including family disputes with Michelle Bolsonaro, the 'tariff shock,' poor polling, and the Centrão bloc (União Brasil, PP, Republicanos) opting for neutrality in party conventions. To respond, the team plans to intensify supermarket and market recordings, comparing current food prices with those from 2019—the first year of Jair Bolsonaro's government—to tap into voter dissatisfaction over the cost of living.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja no mapa o perfil dos eleitores de cada estado
item.description: The TSE released the profile of the Brazilian electorate for the 2026 elections, with 158.8 million eligible voters. São Paulo leads with 34.1 million (21.5% of the total), followed by Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and Bahia. The 40–44 age group is the largest in 17 states, and high school completion is the predominant education level in 22 federative units.

item.title: TSE: mais de 300 mil pessoas cegas devem votar nas eleições de 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) reported that 319,489 visually impaired voters are expected to participate in the 2026 general elections, representing 0.20% of the national electorate. São Paulo has the highest absolute number with 53,192 blind voters, while Tocantins has the highest proportion at 0.33%. Electronic voting machines with tactile writing and reading systems enable their participation, highlighting Brazil’s progress in electoral accessibility since 1996.

item.title: Saiba onde o eleitorado apto a votar em 2026 mais cresceu no Brasil
item.description: The Brazilian electorate for the 2026 elections reached 158.7 million, an increase of 2.3 million since 2022. The North region led in proportional growth (+4.37%), followed by the Central-West (+3.97%), while the Northeast had the largest absolute increase (+1.1 million). The Southeast was the only region to decline (-0.56%), reducing its national share.

item.title: Novo Bolsa Família e celular grátis: o que vem no plano Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposes transforming Bolsa Família into a broader income transfer platform that includes professional training and credit access, maintaining benefits for up to two years for beneficiaries who secure formal employment or open a MEI, with potential cashbacks for courses and cheap microcredit from Caixa. The plan also promises free internet for 70 million women and cellphone distribution for low-income groups, contrasting with market demands for fiscal austerity, as his economic team projects R$ 217 billion in spending cuts by 2027 without specifying funding sources.

item.title: Republicanos anuncia Anthony Garotinho como candidato a governador do Rio
item.description: The Republicans party has nominated Anthony Garotinho as its candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro in 2026, following an internal contest against André Português. Garotinho, a former three-time governor, regained eligibility after the Supreme Federal Court annulled an electoral conviction. The party has also nominated Marcelo Crivella for the Senate.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula sanciona projeto para fortalecer indústria da saúde
item.description: President Lula signed into law Bill 2.583/2020, establishing the National Strategy for the Healthcare Economic-Industrial Complex to strengthen domestic production of medicines, supplies, and health technologies. The ceremony took place at 11 a.m. at the Planalto Palace, attended by Health Minister Alexandre Padilha. The initiative aims to reduce import dependence and boost innovation and technological sovereignty in Brazil’s health sector.

item.title: Valdemar: Falta gesto de Flávio Bolsonaro para encerrar briga com Michelle
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, stated that a gesture from Flávio Bolsonaro is lacking to end the feud with Michelle Bolsonaro, commenting on the internal dispute within the Bolsonarist camp. The remark was made in an interview with UOL News, emphasizing the need for reconciliation among Bolsonaro family members to strengthen the political group.

item.title: Lula brinca e diz que tarifaço é com “Stuckinha”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) joked about the US tariff on Brazilian goods, saying the matter was with 'Stuckinha', the nickname of his official photographer Ricardo Stuckert, while leaving the Planalto Palace for the signing of the National Strategy for the Health Economic-Industrial Complex. The 25% US tariff on Brazilian products takes effect on July 22, and the government expects negotiations with the US to advance only after the October elections, awaiting clarity on Brazil’s political landscape.

item.title: Toffoli manda à PGR queixa-crime de Flávio contra Janones por ser chamado de ‘miliciano’
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Dias Toffoli has ordered the Attorney General's Office (PGR) to rule on a criminal complaint filed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro against federal deputy André Janones for alleged slander, after Janones referred to him as a 'miliciano' and other insults in social media videos between March and June 2026. Bolsonaro seeks at least R$200,000 in moral damages, arguing the statements went beyond political criticism and constituted gratuitous offense. His defense claims parliamentary immunity does not apply because the remarks were made online.

item.title: TCU arquiva processo sobre viagens de Janja
item.description: The TCU archived the investigation into alleged irregularities in the international trips of First Lady Janja, concluding that expenses were regular and there was no misuse of public funds. The decision followed AGU guidance and decrees recognizing the public interest nature of the presidential spouse's role, despite her not holding public office. The specific archiving of the New York trip in September 2025 came after a broader review in process TC 000.031/2025-9, which had already dismissed the accusations as unfounded.

item.title: Vai decolar o 'Aerosalomão', caravana de juízes para a posse de Luis Felipe Salomão no comando do STJ
item.description: A group of judges and appellate judges from Rio de Janeiro, nicknamed 'Aerosalomão', will travel to Brasília on August 19 for the inauguration of Luis Felipe Salomão as the new president of the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) for the 2026-2028 term. Salomão, aged 63, assumes the post following his nomination and Senate approval. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Toffoli manda à PGR queixa-crime de Flávio contra Janones por xingamentos: ‘Miliciano’ e ‘bandido’
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Dias Toffoli has forwarded a criminal complaint filed by presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) against Congressman André Janones for defamation, after Janones called him a 'miliciano' and 'bandido' in videos from March to June. Flávio is also seeking R$20,000 in moral damages. Janones faces a similar lawsuit from Michelle Bolsonaro, who alleges he falsely accused her of receiving 'stolen money' from banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Kim atuará como advogado de Renan nas eleições
item.description: Federal deputy Kim Kataguiri announced he will serve as lawyer for Renan Santos' presidential candidacy in the 2026 elections, following the virtual convention of the Missão party. Renan Santos will run for president with Aroldo Medina as his running mate, according to Kim. The ticket was officially confirmed by the Missão party.

item.title: Eleitorado no exterior registra alta de 31,82% para as Eleições 2026
item.description: The Brazilian electorate abroad increased by 31.82% for the 2026 elections, rising from 697,078 to 918,876 voters, according to TSE data. This represents 0.58% of the total electorate, up from 0.45% in 2022, with 221,863 new voters added. These overseas voters can only participate in the presidential election, while other offices will be decided by voters residing in Brazil.

item.title: PF inicia a segurança de candidatos à Presidência; Flávio Bolsonaro recusa proteção
item.description: The Federal Police launched a national security operation for presidential candidates in the 2026 elections, designed to protect up to ten candidacies with risk-based planning, surveillance technology, and coordination with state and local forces. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) declined the protection, citing distrust in the PF leadership and fears of agent infiltration within his team. The PF confirmed participation is voluntary and that candidates’ decisions will be honored.

item.title: O mais novo entrevero entre aliados de Flávio e Valdemar
item.description: Ideological allies within the PL party expressed discomfort after Valdemar Costa Neto’s interview with Globo, in which he questioned Daniella Marques’ electoral viability as a running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro. He stated she lacks the conditions to join the 2026 presidential ticket.

item.title: Nobel de Economia elogia o Pix e diz que tarifaço “fortalecerá” Lula
item.description: Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman praised Brazil's Pix instant payment system and argued that the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian imports will politically strengthen President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Writing in The New York Times, he suggested the external pressure could foster national unity around Lula's government.

item.title: Número de eleitores cresce e Brasil tem 158,7 milhões aptos a votar
item.description: The number of eligible voters in Brazil has reached 158,745,463, an increase of 2.3 million compared to the 2022 elections, when there were 156,454,011. TSE data shows that 89.01% of the electorate now has biometric registration. The 2026 elections will decide presidential, gubernatorial, federal legislative, and state/district offices.

item.title: Não lembra? Recorda quem ainda está vivo na Sul-Americana, Libertadores, Copa do Brasil e quem disputa o título no Brasileirão
item.description: Following the 2026 World Cup break, Brazilian and South American football enters the decisive stage: the Libertadores has its round of 16 set, featuring matches like Palmeiras vs Cerro Porteño and the sole Brazilian clash Flamengo vs Cruzeiro; the Sudamericana grants direct qualification to Atlético-MG, Botafogo, and São Paulo, while Grêmio, Vasco, Bragantino, and Santos must go through playoffs; the Copa do Brasil reaches the round of 16 with key ties Fluminense vs Vasco and Corinthians vs Internacional; the Brasileirão resumes with Palmeiras leading at 41 points, Flamengo second with 34 (one game in hand), Fluminense third with 32, and Bragantino fourth with 30.

item.title: Marco Rubio usa candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro para se tornar vice-rei do Brasil
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) is portrayed as a candidate backed by Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State, to run for Brazil’s presidency in 2026, aiming to serve U.S. interests through tariff pressure. The text claims that the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods are intended to force openness in high-value sectors and position Bolsonaro as a White House proxy in the Planalto Palace. It criticizes Lula for allegedly prioritizing ego over national interests by refusing to yield to U.S. demands, while arguing that Brazilian sovereignty requires resistance to such external pressure.

item.title: Comissão presidida pelo PT passa o ano sem fiscalizar o governo
item.description: The Financial Oversight and Control Commission (CFFC) of the Chamber of Deputies, chaired by Deputy Alexandre Lindenmeyer (PT-RS), ended 2026 without approving any request for audit, oversight, or summons of federal authorities. The committee, responsible for monitoring public policy execution and the use of federal funds, failed to exercise its oversight function throughout the year.

item.title: A nova baixa na chapa do PL no Rio
item.description: Rogério Lisboa withdrew from the PL's vice-governor ticket in Rio after pressure from Eduardo Paes (PSD), who had already allied with the MDB and nominated Jane Reis as his running mate. This marks the third defection from the Bolsonaro-aligned slate in Rio, following the withdrawals of Cláudio Castro and Márcio Canella from the Senate race due to PF investigations. The PL is racing to finalize its ticket before its Saturday convention to meet the candidate registration deadline.

item.title: Partido Missão antecipa convenção e oficializa Renan Santos como candidato à Presidência
item.description: The Missão Party held an online convention and formally nominated Renan Santos as its presidential candidate for the 2026 elections. The early convention was advised by the pre-campaign security team due to escalating threats from criminal factions, which Santos says he experienced in Ceará, São Paulo, and Rio de Janeiro. The national campaign launch event is set for August 1st, enabling Federal Police involvement, and will feature the presentation of the 'Yellow Book' policy document and Santos’s running mate, Aroldo Medina.

item.title: PF inicia operação de segurança para presidenciáveis; Renan Santos antecipa convenção e Flávio nega escolta
item.description: The Federal Police launched a national security operation for the 2026 presidential candidates, with a R$95 million scheme to protect up to ten contenders. Pre-candidate Renan Santos (Missão) moved up his party convention to today, citing threats from the PCC and CV as justification for requesting police escort. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) refused the PF security detail, saying he does not trust PF chief Andrei Rodrigues and alleging possible infiltration in his campaign, while redirecting agents to INSS fraud investigations.

item.title: Missão oficializa Renan Santos como candidato ao Planalto
item.description: The Missão party advanced its national convention and officially confirmed Renan Santos as its presidential candidate, originally scheduled for August 1. The move was driven by security concerns involving the candidate, according to the party. The announcement was made on Monday, the 20th.

item.title: Eleições 2026: prazo para pedir voto em trânsito começa nesta segunda-feira; veja como fazer
item.description: The deadline to request transit voting for the 2026 Brazilian elections begins this Monday, July 20, and runs until August 20, accessible via the TSE’s Autoatendimento Eleitoral or in person at electoral offices. Voters outside their electoral domicile may vote in another municipality if it is a state capital or has over 100,000 electors: within the same state, they can vote for all offices; outside the state, only for president. Special groups — including poll workers, prison staff, people with disabilities, Indigenous communities, and rural settlers — are eligible, with some having until August 28 to apply.

item.title: As pesquisas desta semana sobre a eleição para presidente
item.description: Lula leads the presidential election polls for 2026 with 40% in recent surveys by Quaest and PoderData, ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro. This week, Real Time Big Data (Tuesday) and Datafolha (Friday) will release new polls with 2,000 and 2,004 interviews, respectively, measuring voting intentions, scenarios of candidate withdrawal, and voter perceptions on issues such as ending the 6×1 workweek, STF ministerial mandates, and the 90-day ban on Flávio Bolsonaro visiting Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Saiba quando cada partido fará sua convenção para definir os candidatos nas eleições
item.description: The partisan convention period for the 2026 Brazilian elections begins on Monday, July 20, and runs until August 5. At least 14 parties have confirmed dates, including the PDT opening the calendar on July 20, the PL launching Flávio Bolsonaro on July 25, the PSD confirming Ronaldo Caiado on July 26, and the PT formalizing Lula’s re-election bid on August 2. The conventions will determine candidates, alliances, and slates, followed by registration with the Electoral Justice.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest mostra que 55% acreditam na vitória de Lula e só 25% de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A Quaest poll shows that 55% of respondents believe Lula will win the 2026 elections, while only 25% expect Flávio Bolsonaro to prevail. This indicates a significant lead for the incumbent president in voter perception, despite lingering Bolsonarist resistance. The data suggests that the narrative of continuity under Lula still resonates with the majority of those surveyed.

item.title: Missão antecipa convenção e oficializa candidatura de Renan Santos por motivo de segurança
item.description: The Mission party advanced its national convention and officially launched Renan Santos' presidential candidacy, originally scheduled for August 1. The move was made for security reasons following threats and intimidation by criminal factions, including the Red Command, in incidents across Ceará, São Paulo, and Rio de Janeiro. The August 1 event will proceed as planned to publicly present the candidacy and release the 'Yellow Book,' detailing campaign proposals on public security, economy, education, infrastructure, and state reform.

item.title: O endurecimento às bets
item.description: The federal government tightened legislation against online betting ('bets') through two ordinances effective July 17, requiring addiction risk warnings and removing 56,000 betting sites/apps and 1,000 influencer profiles, citing public health and household debt concerns. However, the government collected R$12.1 billion in betting taxes by April 2026, while betting spending reached R$30 billion in March, raising doubts about the sincerity of the crackdown amid declining purchasing power and public dissatisfaction. Critics suggest the move is electorally motivated ahead of the 2026 elections, aiming to gain voter favor rather than genuinely addressing gambling addiction.

item.title: Odds Brasileirão 2026: Palmeiras é favorito
item.description: Palmeiras is the favorite in the 2026 Brasileirão title odds across Betano, bet365 and Superbet, followed by Flamengo and Fluminense. The odds reflect the current league standings, with Palmeiras leading and Flamengo in second. The article emphasizes the historical rivalry between Palmeiras and Flamengo, who have won 7 of the last 10 Brasileirões combined.

item.title: “Espanha com camisa vermelha ganha”, diz Lindbergh
item.description: Federal deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT) used Spain’s 1-0 victory over Argentina in the World Cup final to mock Argentine President Javier Milei, linking the result to Brazil’s political landscape. In a post on X, he stated that President Lula (PT) is friends with the Spanish prime minister, implying a symbolic connection between Spain’s win and international support for Lula.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Prioridade processual e força-tarefa de fiscalização começam nesta segunda (20)
item.description: Starting July 20, 2026, electoral procedural priority takes effect in Brazil under the TSE Electoral Calendar, ensuring preferential processing and judgment of all electoral cases until October 30. The measure mobilizes Electoral Justice, the Electoral Public Prosecutor’s Office, and executive and control branches at all government levels to expedite decisions and combat illicit acts before voting and diploma. It is grounded in Article 94 of Law No. 9,504/1997 and Article 61 of TSE Resolution No. 23,608/2019, aiming to prevent deadline losses and forfeiture of rights.

item.title: Renan Santos reage à declaração de Ciro Gomes sobre possível apoio à Presidência: 'Ele é inteligentíssimo, fico lisonjeado'
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for president from the Mission party, responded positively to Ciro Gomes' (PSDB) statement about potentially supporting him in 2026, calling him 'inteligentíssimo' and saying he felt honored. Ciro had mentioned considering support for either Renan or Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) after Aécio Neves withdrew, though he emphasized prioritizing the Ceará gubernatorial race and maintaining alliances across the political spectrum.

item.title: PE: PT coloca ex-aliado de Bolsonaro como suplente de Humberto Costa
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) in Pernambuco has designated federal deputy Luciano Bivar (MDB), a former ally of Jair Bolsonaro, as the alternate for Senator Humberto Costa (PT) in the 2026 Senate race. The decision was made during a meeting in Bom Conselho to strengthen the majoritarian ticket of the Hope Federation (PT/PCdoB/PV). Bivar previously led the PSL and played a key role in Bolsonaro's 2018 election victory before breaking with him in 2019.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral passa a utilizar o mural eletrônico nos processos de registro de candidatura
item.description: Starting today (20), the Electoral Justice will use the electronic bulletin board as the primary means of summoning parties, federations, coalitions, and candidates in the candidacy registration processes for the 2026 General Elections. As established by TSE Resolution No. 23.754/2026, the measure will remain in effect until December 19, 2026, with summonses considered valid upon publication on the electronic bulletin board, triggering the start of procedural deadlines. Political entities and candidates are advised to monitor the bulletin board regularly and keep their contact information updated to avoid missing deadlines.

item.title: Saiba quais pesquisas serão divulgadas nesta 2ª feira
item.description: Poder360 released a list of electoral polls that may be published starting Monday, July 20, 2026, based on TSE records. The surveys cover Alagoas, Distrito Federal, Rio Grande do Norte, and Rio Grande do Sul, commissioned by media outlets, consultancies, and research institutes. Publication is contingent on meeting the legal minimum waiting period and registration with the Electoral Justice.

item.title: Milei vai se encontrar com Tarcísio em São Paulo durante visita ao Brasil
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei will meet with São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas on Saturday (2) ahead of the PL convention that will formalize Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential candidacy. Milei will not be able to visit jailed former President Bolsonaro due to a STF suspension on social visits, nor is he expected to meet with Lula. The meeting highlights growing alignment between conservative leaders in Argentina and Brazil amid right-wing fragmentation ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa desiste de concorrer à Presidência
item.description: Former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa withdrew from the 2026 presidential race after conditions for his candidacy were not met, informing his party, the Christian Democracy (DC). Despite his withdrawal, the DC leadership is attempting to keep him in the race, while Aldo Rebelo continues to claim he is the party's pre-candidate, a claim rejected by DC president João Caldas. Barbosa, the first Black justice on the STF, has been speculated as a presidential candidate since 2013 but never solidified a run.

item.title: Remessas internacionais batem recorde de R$ 2,6 bilhões
item.description: International remittances processed under Brazil's Remessa Conforme program reached R$ 2.6 billion in June 2026, the highest monthly value since the program's launch in 2023, driven by MP 1.357/2026 which eliminated the 20% federal import tax on purchases under US$ 50. The figure marks a 37% increase from May and a 116% annual rise in package volume, with 27.4 million shipments recorded. While the program shows strong growth, retail and industry groups criticize the measure as politically motivated and call for its repeal or extension of tax exemptions to domestically produced goods.

item.title: Do tarifaço às urnas: a leitura do Planalto sobre a ofensiva comercial de Trump
item.description: The Brazilian government assesses that the 2026 presidential elections in both Brazil and the U.S. are likely to reduce prospects for relief from Trump’s new tariffs, especially as Secretary of State Marco Rubio publicly backs Flávio Bolsonaro and blames Lula for the measures. While negotiations continue to expand tariff exemptions, there is no expectation of progress due to the U.S. alignment with Brazil’s opposition. Officials also track U.S. legislative elections, anticipating a possible Democratic win in the House, which could heighten political pressure on Trump.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que vai abrir mão de segurança da PF durante campanha eleitoral
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) announced he will not use Federal Police security during his 2026 presidential campaign, citing distrust in current PF Director Andrei Passos Rodrigues and fear of infiltrators in his team. He requested that PF agents be redirected to investigate alleged fraud against INSS retirees and the alleged involvement of Fábio Luís Lula da Silva (Lulinha) in corruption schemes. The PF begins on Monday (20) a protection operation for presidential candidates, deploying up to 458 agents, armored vehicles, anti-drone equipment, and bomb detection kits, with a budget of R$ 95 million.

item.title: Lindbergh associa título da Espanha ao PT: "Camisa vermelha ganha"
item.description: Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) celebrated Spain’s victory over Argentina in the 2026 World Cup final, linking the team’s red jersey to the PT and interpreting the win as a positive omen for Brazil’s 2026 presidential elections. He highlighted the friendship between Lula and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, both left-wing leaders, and criticized Argentine President Javier Milei for the country’s economic crisis, quoting Lionel Messi on the struggle to make ends meet. Lindbergh also mocked Milei, Bolsonaro, and Trump, saying they 'should cry'.

item.title: Tarifas de Trump não vão funcionar e fortalecerão Lula, diz Nobel de Economia
item.description: Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman argues that Trump's tariffs on Brazil will be economically ineffective and will instead strengthen President Lula politically. He condemns the tariffs as an unjust punishment for Brazil's success with PIX, which he calls 'the money of the future,' and for its democratic consolidation, contrasting with the U.S., where Bolsonaro was prosecuted for attempting a coup. Krugman also links the hostility toward PIX to the Trump administration's broader opposition to progress that threatens the interests of oligarchic donors.

item.title: Justiça Eleitoral abre prazo para eleitor solicitar voto em trânsito; saiba como
item.description: The Electoral Justice has opened the deadline for requesting absentee voting until August 20, allowing voters away from their electoral residence on election day to vote temporarily in another locality. Absentee voting permits voting for all offices if within the same state, or only for president if in another state, and also applies to specific groups such as pretrial detainees, military personnel, security agents, people with disabilities, indigenous peoples, quilombolas, and election workers.
